column2: This workbook adds CIF-derived functional-group typing for HOF-protein recommender development.
Bonds are inferred from interatomic distances using covalent radii plus tolerance because CIF files generally do not encode formal bond orders.

The layer detects carboxylate/carboxylic-acid-like groups, hydroxyl, ether, carbonyl, amide-like groups, amine, imine, pyridine-like N, sulfonate/sulfate, phosphate/phosphonate, aromatic rings, and C-halogen groups.
Donor and acceptor counts are group-derived estimates. They are stronger than heteroatom proxies but still depend on inferred bonding and explicit H availability.
Many CIFs omit H atoms. When explicit H atoms are absent, donor typing and protonation-state distinction are incomplete.
Metal-ligand contacts are flagged because coordination environments can affect donor/acceptor behaviour.
Aromatic rings are detected using approximate ring-size and bond-distance rules, not formal cheminformatics aromaticity perception.
Use hof_functional_interaction_score as a HOF-side chemistry layer and pairwise_functional_complementarity_score as a protein-specific functional matching layer.
Combine functional group typing with atom/pore accessibility so that surface- or pore-exposed functional groups receive stronger weight than buried groups.
